key_insight: A solver-guided LLM can learn to choose the best MIP formulation for each multi-warehouse inventory instance, improving allocation quality beyond any single fixed formulation.
engineering_relevance: This enables adaptive optimization pipelines that match formulation choice to instance characteristics like demand concentration, imbalance, scale, service constraints, and volatility.
method: Build a candidate library of OR experts, where each expert is a solver-executable MIP formulation with a different allocation priority.
Create balanced supervised fine-tuning records, then convert solver-evaluated quality gaps into margin-weighted IPO preferences and reward metadata.
Use GRPO to train the selector to pick the best formulation per instance based on solver feedback.
evidence_signal: On JD.com inventory allocation instances, GRPO raised Hit Ratio@1 from 21.45% to 50.42% and Hit Ratio@2 from 70.47% to 82.31%, improving allocation accuracy by 12.57 percentage points and narrowing the oracle gap to 4.85 points.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable solver-evaluated labels and may be sensitive to candidate-formulation coverage, reward design, and compute cost during training.
paper_title: Large Language Model for Operations Research Formulation Selection in Multi-Warehouse Inventory Allocation
